transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Diego Rios (CSM), Priya Nair (SE), Marcus Lee (Crestline Head of Product), Anita Singh (VP Eng), Jonas Petrov (DevOps), Leah Ortiz (Data Scientist)
Links shared: QBR deck (drive link), cost spreadsheet (sheets.link/crestline-costs), security packet (drive.link/crestline-soc2)

Summary: Quick QBR / health check to review usage trends, cost, recent reliability blips during promo week, and discuss Dedicated pilot sizing and security artifacts.

--- Transcript (timestamps are approximate, auto-transcribed) ---
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes on the calendar. Quick round robin, say hi.
[00:06] Marcus: Hey, Marcus here. We'll try to keep it focused, got some folks pulled in from eng.
[00:09] Anita: Anita, VP Engineering, thanks.
[00:11] Jonas: Jonas on infra.
[00:12] Leah: Leah, data science.
[00:14] Diego: Diego from Redwood CSM.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, SE.
[00:17] Lena: Cool. Agenda \u0014 usage & cost, reliability incidents, roadmap options (hosted vs dedicated), security ask, then next steps.

[02:00] Lena: Diego, can you kick off with the usage trend?
[02:05] Diego: Yeah, sure: so over the last quarter we've seen a ~43% increase in token volume month over month, basically driven by two things: new conversational flows in checkout and expanded summarization for product docs. The sheet I shared breaks down per-route token counts, see the costs tab, the per-token unit cost is up because of longer sequences and more embeddings.
[02:35] Marcus: Sorry quick question, the tokens that are billed for embeddings - we saw a jump in embedding calls last month\u000094are those the longer vector embeddings or are you counting the embed + metadata tokens?
[02:45] Diego: The export includes both; the embeddings are billed per-embedding-unit in the sheet, but you can see the underlying tokenization in the raw csv. There's a note about batching savings we recommended \u0014 you get up to 35% cost reduction if you batch user sessions into a single call.

[05:00] Jonas: During the promo week we hit a couple latency spikes around 11am UTC; our SRE saw timeouts on the hosted route and some retries, looking at logs it correlated with a big burst of long-context generations. Any ideas on fallback?
[05:20] Priya: Yep, that's consistent with what we've seen on similar customers. The routing policy default will try hosted first; if you set an autoscaling/burst policy or pin to a dedicated pool you reduce that noisy neighbor effect. Also KV cache/prefix caching can reduce cost and latency by avoiding re-generation for repeated prompts.
[05:45] Marcus: When you say dedicated pool, does that mean we get pinned GPUs or is it a soft reservation? We talked about Redwood Dedicated but unclear on the level of isolation.
[05:55] Lena: Good question. For Dedicated we provide reserved capacity \u0014 you get dedicated GPU pools for your account and predictable throughput; there are autoscaling configs but capacity is yours. We can share the SLA and the sizing guide.

[07:10] Anita: From a procurement angle we need to see SOC2 and ISO artifacts plus KMS diagrams, and clarity on key rotation and HSM. Also SSO and RBAC model.
[07:25] Priya: Absolutely \u0014 I'll upload SOC 2 and ISO docs and a KMS/arch diagram after the call. For SSO we support SAML/Okta and can map to RBAC roles; audit logs are available in the console and exportable.
[07:45] Anita: And the retention on logs? We may need 1 year for audit.
[07:49] Priya: We have configurable retention \u0014 by default 90 days, enterprise add-on for 1 year or longer. I'll include that in the security packet.

[09:00] Leah: On the embedding quality note \u0014 we've been seeing drift with one of your new quantized models, embeddings are slightly less consistent for near-neighbor recall, so a few false negatives in search. We filed a ticket but wanted to discuss if there's a recommended model or quantization profile to revert to.
[09:20] Priya: Thanks, Leah. We did push a quantized variant (q4_2) to reduce cost, there are tradeoffs for recall. For high accuracy you can pin to the float or q8 profile; or we can run an embedding eval comparing q2/q4/q8 and the full float model on your holdout set.
[09:45] Leah: That would be great \u0014 a quick notebook + numbers so we can make a decision.

[11:00] Marcus: Cost is also a concern, even with batching suggestions the month-over-month spend is up 60% on tokens. Can we get a projected TCO if we move 40% of steady-state traffic to Dedicated?
[11:16] Diego: We can do a Dedicated sizing + cost model, yes. Typical lift is lower per-token cost at scale because of lower per-token infra overhead, plus you get predictable throughput. I'll pull together a model with your current 3-months of traffic and show a few commit levels.

[13:00] Jonas: Operationally, if we go Dedicated, what's the rollback if we see quality or latency regressions? Is there an automatic fallback to hosted?
[13:10] Priya: Yes \u0014 the routing policies can be set to failover to hosted variants. We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback rules. Also, we normally recommend a staged rollout: pilot on a subset of routes, compare latency/cost/quality, then expand.

[15:00] Lena: Quick note on SLAs \u0014 for Dedicated we have uptime SLAs and latency targets baked into the contract; I'll send the SLA PDF.

[16:00] Marcus: We had a short incident in March where a rate limit misconfiguration blocked some internal services, that was our mistake but wanted to confirm how quotas work and alerting.
[16:15] Diego: There are two layers \u0014 per-account quotas and per-route limits. You can configure alerts in the Console; we can also set up PagerDuty hooks for critical thresholds. I'll propose thresholds based on your peak.

[18:00] Anita: On roadmap timing \u0014 if we want Dedicated by early June, when do we need to sign off?
[18:10] Lena: For a June deployment we should lock a term by mid-May to allow capacity planning and any network setup (VPC peering). So target sign-off by 2026-05-15.

[19:30] Jonas: On the VPC setup \u0014 are there VPN options or only VPC peering? We have an on-prem cluster sometimes used for compliance lanes.
[19:45] Priya: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink in supported cloud regions, and an on-prem package for air-gapped installs; specifics depend on the deployment. I'll include the network options and a template network diagram in the packet.

[22:00] Leah: Also want to call out model drift monitoring \u0014 any built-in alerting if generation quality degrades?
[22:12] Diego: We have quality monitoring in Redwood Optimize \u0014 you can bind eval sets and get regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We can run a baseline eval for your top 20 prompts.

[24:00] Marcus: Ok, let's prioritize: 1) costs + usage export; 2) security doc + KMS + retention; 3) Dedicated sizing call; 4) embedding eval. Anything else?
[24:10] Anita: Procurement will also need the contract redline and liability limits.
[24:15] Lena: We'll triage that with legal, but I can get standard redline terms to your procurement rep.

[26:00] Priya: Quick technical aside \u0014 the latency spikes looked like long-context workloads pushing KV cache thrash; if you can increase KV cache retention and enable prefix caching on the session route you'll see fewer backend hits for repeated histories. Also reduce sequence length where possible.
[26:25] Jonas: We'll have to tweak frontend behavior to truncate user history earlier, yes.

[28:00] Leah: On embeddings, I can share a 500-sample holdout set for the eval. Do you prefer a csv or parquet?
[28:10] Priya: CSV is fine, include doc ids and expected nearest neighbor ids. We'll run similarity recall and ROC metrics.

[30:00] Lena: Great \u0014 to recap at a high level: Diego sends usage export and cost model; Priya uploads security artifacts and KMS/arch; Lena & Jonas schedule Dedicated sizing call and target mid-April to mid-May sign-off; Leah & Priya run embedding eval.

[31:00] Marcus: timeline check \u0014 Diego, can you have the cost model by Friday?
[31:06] Diego: Yes, I'll send a draft by 2026-04-09 EOD.

[32:00] Anita: Procurement will expect contract terms referenced by 2026-05-01, can you confirm legal contact?
[32:06] Lena: I'll introduce you to our legal contact after this call.

[33:30] Jonas: One more ops question \u0014 if we pin to Dedicated and later want to scale down, what's the commitment window?
[33:40] Lena: Commit windows vary by plan; typical reserved capacity is monthly or annual with options for change windows. I'll include a sample commit / change policy in the pricing doc.

[36:00] (brief cross-talk about scheduling and timezone)
[37:00] Priya: I'll attach network diagrams and a sample VPC peering checklist. Also adding a note on key rotation frequency and HSM options.

[39:00] Leah: Thanks \u0014 we'll share the holdout set and any tickets for embedding drift.

[40:30] Marcus: Thanks everyone, this was helpful. Any other blockers?
[40:35] Anita: No blockers.
[40:40] Lena: Alright we'll follow up with the artifacts and book the Dedicated sizing session. Thanks all.
[41:00] Diego: Thanks, bye.
[41:10] Priya: Thanks, bye.

--- End transcript ---

Notes on transcription: occasional misheard product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate"), filler words and overlaps. Action items captured above.
